The '''2022–23 season''' was [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s 31st season in the [[Premier League]], 45th consecutive season in the top flight of the [[English football league system]] and 141st season in existence. In addition to the [[2022–23 Premier League|domestic league]], they participated in the season's [[2022–23 FA Cup|FA Cup]], [[2022–23 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] and [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], having finished fourth in the [[2021–22 Premier League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Tottenham secure Champions League qualification ahead of Arsenal |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3490811/2022/05/22/tottenham-secure-champions-league-qualification-ahead-of-arsenal/ |website=The Athletic |date=22 May 2022 |access-date=28 May 2023 |first=Luke |last=Brown}}</ref>

On 26 March 2023, Tottenham announced that head coach [[Antonio Conte]] had left the club by mutual agreement. On the same day, [[Cristian Stellini]] took charge as the acting head coach until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Club announcement – Antonio departs|url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2023/march/club-announcement-antonio-departs/|work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|date=26 March 2023|access-date=26 March 2023}}</ref> On 24 April 2023, following a 6–1 loss to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], Stellini was sacked and replaced by [[Ryan Mason]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Club update from Daniel |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2023/april/club-update-from-daniel/ |work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=24 April 2023 |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Coaching update |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2023/april/coaching-update/ |work=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=25 April 2023 |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref>

==Season overview==
[[File:20150616 Antonio Conte.jpg|160px|thumb|[[Antonio Conte]], manager of Tottenham Hotspur until 26 March 2023|alt=A coloured photograph of Antonio Conte]]
Tottenham's season started with a 4–1 home win against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Tottenham Hotspur 4–1 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62358043 |work=BBC Sport |first=Alex |last=Bysouth |date=6 August 2022 |access-date=27 April 2023}}</ref> The club then went on a seven-game unbeaten run in the league, which saw Tottenham beat [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] 6–2 with [[Son Heung-min]] coming off the bench to score a second half hat-trick.<ref>{{cite news |title=Heung-min Son steals the show for Tottenham with 31-minute hat-trick that takes him level with Cristiano Ronaldo record |url=https://talksport.com/football/1197537/heung-min-son-tottenham-leicester-cristiano-ronaldo/ |work=TalkSport |date=17 September 2022 |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref> After the international break, the players returned for an away game on 1 October against [[North London derby|North London rivals]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] losing 3–1 and ending their Premier League undefeated streak.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal 3–1 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/63017880 |work=BBC Sport |first=Phil |last=McNulty |date=1 October 2022 |access-date=22 May 2023}}</ref> Tottenham went on to win their next two matches against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] and [[Everton F.C|Everton]]; however, their form dropped with multiple losses in the league in October and November against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]. On the final game before the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] break, Tottenham defeated [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] 4–3.

In the Champions League, Tottenham had good enough form to top their group with a double win over [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and a home win against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]]. Their only loss was away to [[Sporting CP]] in Portugal. For the round of 16, Tottenham were drawn against seven-time winners [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]], to be played in February and March 2023.

Tottenham entered the third round of the EFL Cup and were drawn away to [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]]. Forest at the time were bottom of the league and struggling to find form. The match took place on 9 November, and Tottenham started with what was considered a strong squad. However, the game resulted in a 2–0 defeat, with goals from [[Renan Lodi]] and [[Jesse Lingard]] knocking the club out of the competition.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63481005 |title=Carabao Cup: Nottingham Forest 2–0 Tottenham Hotspur |work=BBC Sport |first=Emma |last=Smith |date=9 November 2022 |access-date=25 April 2023}}</ref>

The winter break came early due to the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar. After the World Cup, Tottenham only played one game in December, against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], which ended as a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64022707 |title=Brentford 2–2 Tottenham |work=BBC Sport |first=Michael |last=Emons |date=26 December 2022 |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref>

In January and February, Tottenham's league form was up and down. They first lost 2–0 at home to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on New Year's Day, but then thrashed [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] 4–0. Tottenham then had a difficult run of games against Arsenal, [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] and then Manchester City again.

Tottenham advanced to the fifth round of the FA Cup defeating [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] 1–0 in the third round,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/34651/12779953/tottenham-1-0-portsmouth-harry-kane-nets-265th-tottenham-goal-to-send-spurs-through-to-fa-cup-fourth-round |title=Tottenham 1-0 Portsmouth: Harry Kane nets 265th Tottenham goal to send Spurs through to FA Cup fourth round |work=SkySports |date=7 January 2023 |access-date=26 April 2023}}</ref> and defeating [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] 3–0 in the fourth round.

In February, Conte returned to Italy to have surgery to remove his [[gallbladder]], leaving [[Cristian Stellini]] in charge. Under Stellini, Tottenham played their round of 16 Champions League match, first away in Milan, losing 1–0. The home game played on 8 March was a goalless draw, knocking Tottenham out of the Champions League. The game also saw [[Cristian Romero (footballer, born 1998)|Cristian Romero]] get sent off for a second yellow card.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/64881080 |title=Tottenham 0 – 0 Milan |work=BBC Sport |first=Phil |last=McNulty |date=8 March 2023 |accessdate=27 April 2023}}</ref>

Stellini's Tottenham had mixed results, including being knocked out of the FA Cup by [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11675/12827941/antonio-conte-returning-tottenham-boss-says-he-underestimated-recovery-time-following-gallbladder-surgery#:~:text=Conte%20was%20initially%20ruled%20out,and%20undergo%20a%20full%20recovery. |title=Antonio Conte: Returning Tottenham boss says he underestimated recovery time following gallbladder surgery |work=Sky Sports |date=8 March 2023 |accessdate=25 April 2023 }}</ref> On 26 March, Conte was sacked a day after showing his frustration in a news conference after a 3–3 draw at Southampton. Stellini was only in charge for four more games, the last being a crushing 6–1 loss at [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]], Tottenham's worst defeat of the season, after which Stellini was sacked and replaced with assistant coach Ryan Mason.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65366233 |title=Newcastle 6-1 Tottenham: Champions League showdown that was a humiliation |work=BBC Sport |first=Emlyn |last=Begley |date=23 April 2023 |accessdate=30 May 2023 }}</ref> Mason was in charge for six games, winning two, losing three and drawing one. On the last day of the season, Tottenham beat [[Leeds United F.C|Leeds United]] 4–1 away from home and finishing in eighth place, the club's worst league position since the [[2008–09 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2008–09 season]]. This was also [[Lucas Moura]]'s last game for the club, as he scored the final goal of the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65661818 |title=Leeds United 1–4 Tottenham Hotspur |work=BBC Sport |first=Simon |last=Stone |date=28 May 2023 |accessdate=30 May 2023 }}</ref>

==Pre-season and friendlies==
To prepare for the upcoming season, Tottenham played a series of [[Friendly matches|friendlies]] across the world. The club first met Korean club [[K League 1|Team K League]] and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in South Korea for the Coupang Play Series on 13 and 16 July 2022, respectively.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/april/club-to-face-team-k-league-in-opening-korea-tour-match/ |title=Club to face Team K League in opening Korea Tour match |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=13 April 2022 |access-date=14 April 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/may/sevilla-announced-as-second-korea-tour-opponents/ |title=Sevilla announced as second Korea Tour opponents |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=23 May 2022 |access-date=23 May 2022 }}</ref> The team then travelled to Scotland to play [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 23 July 2022<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/april/rangers-announced-as-pre-season-opponents/ |title=Rangers announced as pre-season opponents |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=26 April 2022 |access-date=27 April 2022 }}</ref> and played [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] in Israel for the I-Tech Cup the following week.<ref>{{cite news |title=Club to face AS Roma in Israel |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/may/club-to-face-as-roma-in-israel/ |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=27 May 2022 |access-date=27 May 2022 }}</ref>

In December, while the season was halted due to the ongoing [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], Tottenham announced a mid-season friendly [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] against Scottish side [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] on 9 December as well as an additional match at home with reduced capacity to French club [[OGC Nice|Nice]] on 21 December 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Men's first team to face Motherwell in behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/december/men-s-first-team-to-face-motherwell-in-behind-closed-doors-friendly-on-friday-live-on-spursplay/ |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=6 December 2022 |access-date=6 December 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Spurs take on OGC Nice in exhibition match at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/december/spurs-take-on-ogc-nice-in-exhibition-match-at-tottenham-hotspur-stadium/ |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=7 December 2022 |access-date=7 December 2022 }}</ref>

===FA Cup===
{{main|2022–23 FA Cup}}

Tottenham entered the FA Cup in the third round and were drawn at home to [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth at home in FA Cup |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2022/november/fa-cup-third-round-draw-details/ |access-date=28 November 2022 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=28 November 2022}}</ref> They were then drawn away to [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] in the fourth round,<ref>{{cite news |title=Preston away in FA Cup |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2023/january/fa-cup-fourth-round-draw-details/ |access-date=8 January 2023 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=8 January 2023}}</ref> and away to [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] in the fifth round.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sheffield United away in FA Cup fifth round |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/2023/february/sheffield-united-away-in-fa-cup-fifth-round/ |access-date=8 February 2023 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C. |date=7 February 2023}}</ref>
